label: Runtime & infrastructure
note: The layer the pipelines run on: process management, storage, attention kernels, the two ComfyUI instances, delivery and the boards. Swaps here are rarely about quality — they are about a thing that silently did not work.

entities.name: Ad-hoc launchers (kill_port + Popen)
entities.summary: Services were started by killing whatever held the port and spawning a child process.

issues.text: Nothing was restartable or supervised; a crash was invisible.

entities.name: systemd user units
entities.summary: Every service became a unit, which is why a restart is now a one-line operation. It also introduced a failure mode that looks like a broken model.

issues.text: Made services restartable and supervised.

crewai-gui.service has Wants=comfyui.service, so EVERY GUI restart pulls in a ComfyUI start that crash-loops against an orphan holding :8188 until the start limit — the unit starts were not someone fixing ComfyUI. Service state must be read as port ownership by cgroup BEFORE unit state.
crewai-gui is a SYSTEM unit, so it cannot order itself after the user-level Postgres; the connection pool's lazy open and retry covers boot ordering instead.
The executor sandbox refuses sudo, so a unit restart inside a task has to be handed back to the creator.

entities.name: Pause / resume registry
entities.summary: Before this a run could only be halted. Now there is a scoped registry with stage-level resume.

issues.text: Halt-only control meant a stopped run lost everything done so far.

entities.name: JSON / JSONL state files
entities.summary: 52,582 JSON/JSONL files and 1.15 GB in data/. Measured, not estimated, in the 10-01 audit that started the database migration.

issues.text: prompt_log.json (37.1 MB, capped at exactly 10,000 entries with the cap already binding) read one pipeline in 81 ms and appended one entry in 185 ms, against 0.5 ms / 21 ms in SQLite.
The write path was a bare open(path,'w') truncate, so those 185 ms are a corruption window — and the reader's bare except hid the loss.
Worse offenders remain: asset_library_instruments_meta.json is 62.5 MB / 66,028 entries rebuilt whole per call, and 563 pipeline state files (127 MB) are parsed up to 200 at a time per request.
Write safety is still split across ~505 bare truncate sites against ~133 atomic tmp+os.replace and 12 modules using flock.

entities.name: SQLite
entities.summary: Recommended as the first step because it was already in the program and needs no server. It held three live DBs for one day before the operator chose Postgres.

issues.text: Fixed the JSON read/write cost immediately (prompt_log 185 ms → 21 ms) with no new service to run.
Single-writer: the advice was 'Postgres when several processes need to write at once', which is this program's shape.
The retired files are RENAMED *.pre-postgres-20261002 and never deleted — a fresh .sqlite3 appearing in data/runtime means a missed import sqlite3 path.

entities.name: Postgres 16.15
entities.where: ~/pg16 (micromamba), zyg-postgres.service, unix socket only, pgdb.py + crews/alembic
entities.summary: Installed WITHOUT root via micromamba, listening on a unix socket with no TCP. Schema is owned by Alembic; modules never CREATE TABLE and all access goes through pgdb.py.

issues.text: Cutover verified rather than assumed: final sync 0 new rows, --verify compared id sets (553/3119/3579/24/111/2028 all OK) and no fresh .sqlite3 appeared.
A dead server costs callers microseconds for 15 s via a down-marker instead of a 10 s wait each; call sites already degrade.
The FIRST ping() on an unreachable DSN still costs the full 10 s pool.open timeout before the down-marker kicks in.
Installed with the disk at 99% (34 GB free) — ~/pg16/data/log growth is unwatched.

entities.name: MongoDB
entities.summary: Rejected on the reasoning that produced the problem in the first place: the JSON-document habit is what created 52k files, and the data is genuinely relational.

issues.text: No measured win for this workload, and a document store would have re-created the storage shape being migrated away from.

entities.name: TeaCache
entities.summary: Retired because it was import-dead: it had not been running at all.

issues.text: Import-dead — a speed feature nobody was getting. Found by audit, not by a symptom.

entities.name: SageAttention (triton)
entities.summary: The triton build of SageAttention, switched on by env for the Wan path.

issues.text: The SageAttention 2.2 CUDA build needs nvcc, which is not installed system-wide — so the stack runs the triton build.

entities.name: ComfyUI 0.22 (:8188)
entities.summary: The production instance, carrying hand-written queue-survival patches in main.py and model_management.py. Deliberately NOT upgraded: an 0.22→0.28 jump would conflict exactly where those patches live.

issues.text: It accepts unknown inputs SILENTLY — writing seed/steps/cfg onto the wrong sampler node is inert, and the graph runs looking correct.
It leaves omitted workflow inputs as None rather than defaulting them.
LoraLoader silently applied NOTHING for PEFT-format LoRAs, logging one line per tensor — 453,440 lines. The verification rule is now a COUNT: 'lora key not loaded' must not rise after a submit.
Cannot be upgraded in place: the local clone is depth-1 shallow with 0 tags, and 'take upstream' in model_management.py would delete the queue-survival patches.
An orphan process from an interactive session held :8188 for four days while the health probe saw a healthy port.

entities.name: ComfyUI 0.38.1 (:8189)
entities.role: second graph runtime for the new engines
entities.summary: A second instance with its own venv, sharing the production weights library, so LTX-2.5 and HiDream could be adopted without touching the patched production runtime. The two never run GPU work at once.

issues.text: Let a new engine be adopted without upgrading, and therefore without breaking, the production instance.
Started with nohup, not a unit: a user systemd unit was refused by the auto-mode classifier, so comfyui-ltx.service does not exist and the operator has to add it.
Both instances must share one GPU, so :8189 work runs under the production lock.

entities.name: onboard
entities.summary: Replaced because it segfaults on python3.12.

issues.text: Segfaults on python3.12.

entities.name: xvkbd
entities.summary: The working on-screen keyboard for the streamed desktop.

entities.name: HLS + hls.js
entities.summary: Replaced direct file playback because the browser caps preload at 2.4 s — a limit no server-side change could have fixed.

issues.text: Direct file playback stalled: the browser caps preload at 2.4 s.

entities.name: ffmpeg + NVENC
entities.summary: A pre-July survivor doing more work than any model: every mux, crop, loudness pass and Ken-Burns render. Camera moves that LTX cannot be trusted with are done here instead.

issues.text: Ken-Burns/NVENC throughput caps at 8 concurrent jobs.
The limiter must run BEFORE loudnorm, or scene audio levels come out wrong.
It is the fix for LTX inventing camera moves: the move is never prompted, it is cropped in afterwards.

entities.name: metrics_hub.py (:5000/metrics)
entities.summary: The rebuilt metrics hub: mtime-cached collectors, hot-reloaded without a GUI restart, 454 ms cold against the old hub's 11.7 s. This lineage tab is a section of it.

issues.text: The old hub was structurally wrong, not just slow: success meant 'has an ended timestamp' (kidsmusic read 0% with 61 completed runs), 95 of 170 character records were synthesized backfills counted as real runs, spend read a dead rolling file, and Haiku was priced 4x low.
Eight of the eleven subtabs have no automatic poll, so their 'Checked' badge is only as fresh as the last Refresh.

entities.name: HF cache + uv venvs (weights on disk)
entities.role: how weights and environments are stored
entities.summary: One shared weights library plus per-engine venvs. Six disk audits produced rules that are not obvious and have each cost real time.

issues.text: The uv cache HARDLINKS into venvs, so du double-counts and deleting the cache frees almost nothing.
HF blob names ARE sha256, so same-size blobs in one repo are shards, not duplicates — and deleting a weight cache does not disable an engine, because guards test the VENV.
A disk sweep deleted the Chatterbox venv and silently removed the only TTS fallback, which later cost an episode.

For the crews repo use `git prune`, NOT `git gc` — gc needs 48 GB of headroom to repack, while prune freed 4.78 GiB of loose objects with history intact. The orphans come from auto_snapshot.py losing a race with creator_nexus state files.

entities.name: Kanban board (kanban_server.py)
entities.summary: The board every pipeline reports to, and the only place a creator may edit a running task's brief or verifier.

issues.text: Card TITLES are the join keys into the server's stage map, so renaming an engine on a card silently queues the whole department — 24 of 28 documentary cards could never leave queued after the music swap.
It showed only ONE run until other_runs/live_runs and ?pipeline_id= focus were added.
The Videos scan SKIPS every path containing the word 'medusa' (a swimwear-app guard), so clips must be named around it.
A restart kills any live drawing assistant job — /assistant/active must read 0 first.
